name: decision-log
context: Agent systems that must explain or audit why a particular action was taken after the fact. Action-only logs leave reviewers unable to reconstruct the agent's reasoning — the decision log persists the agent's reasoning trace alongside its actions so that post-hoc review, debugging, or compliance auditing can trace any output back to the specific decision that produced it.
benefits: Enables post-hoc explanation of agent behavior for debugging and compliance
Distinguishes a bad decision from a bad outcome — critical for incident analysis
Supports audit trails required in regulated industries
Provides evidence for dispute resolution and human review
tradeoffs: Storage and privacy implications for retaining full reasoning traces
Logging every decision adds latency to the agent loop
Reasoning logs without a review process become shelfware
Large reasoning traces can dominate storage costs
use_cases: Compliance audit: reconstruct why an agent approved or rejected a loan application
Incident response: trace a production failure back to the specific tool call and reasoning step
Customer dispute: show exactly what information the agent based its response on
Performance review: analyze decision patterns to identify systematic biases
avoid_when: No requirement to explain or audit agent decisions
Privacy constraints prohibit retaining reasoning traces
The agent loop is so fast that logging adds meaningful overhead
technology_stack: Vector DB for reasoning trace retrieval
anti_patterns: Logging actions without corresponding reasoning — leaves no explanation
Rewriting reasoning logs after the fact — destroys auditability
Retaining logs without any review process or query mechanism
Head-based/random sampling discards traces you most need (errors, slow calls)
design_principles: Every consequential action must have a corresponding decision-log entry
Logs must be append-only — the agent cannot rewrite its own history
The log entry must include the specific context (evidence, constraints, alternatives considered) that led to the decision
best_practices: Link each action record to the specific reasoning step that caused it
Distinguish key decisions from routine steps — not every token needs a log entry
Index logs by request ID and decision type for efficient post-hoc retrieval
Use tail-based sampling: retain errors, high latency, guardrail triggers
Attach evaluation scores (faithfulness, groundedness, relevance) to each span at capture time
references: Agent Patterns Catalog, Decision Log pattern — https://www.agentpatternscatalog.org/patterns/decision-log/
